# Loading in the data ####
df <- read.csv('../../Data/GradSchool_Admissions.csv')

Univariate Explorations

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = as.factor(admit))) +
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(stat = "count",
            aes(label = after_stat(count)), 
            vjust = 1.5,
            color = 'white') +
  labs(title = "Counts of each admittance status")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gre)) +
  geom_density(fill = 'grey') +
  labs(title = "Distribution of GRE Scores")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gre)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of GRE Scores")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gpa)) + 
  geom_density(fill = 'grey') +
  labs(title = "Distribution of GPA")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gpa)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of GPA Scores")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = rank)) + 
  geom_bar() +
  geom_text(stat = "count",
            aes(label = after_stat(count)), 
            vjust = 1.5,
            color = 'white') +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Rank")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = rank)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Rank")

Bivariate Analysis

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gre, y = admit, group = admit)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplots of Admittance by GRE Scores")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gre, 
             color = as.factor(admit),
             fill = as.factor(admit)
             )) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Density plots of Admittance by GRE Scores",
       color = 'Admittance',
       fill = 'Admittance')

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gpa, y = admit, group = admit)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Boxplots of Admittance by GPA")

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gpa, 
             color = as.factor(admit),
             fill = as.factor(admit)
  )) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Density plots of Admittance by GPA",
       color = 'Admittance',
       fill = 'Admittance')

df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, 
             fill = as.factor(admit))) + 
  geom_bar(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_text(
    stat = "count",
    aes(label = after_stat(count), group = as.factor(admit)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    vjust = 1.5,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Rank with Admittance",
    fill = "Admittance"
  )

Linear Modeling

# Linear models 
lin_1 <- glm(admit~gre, data = df)
summary(lin_1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ gre, data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) -0.1198407  0.1190510  -1.007 0.314722    
## gre          0.0007442  0.0001988   3.744 0.000208 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.2103746)
## 
##     Null deviance: 86.677  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 83.729  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 515.6
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2
lin_2 <- glm(admit~gpa, data = df)
summary(lin_2)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ gpa, data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) -0.42238    0.20606  -2.050 0.041037 *  
## gpa          0.21826    0.06041   3.613 0.000341 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.210866)
## 
##     Null deviance: 86.677  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 83.925  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 516.53
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2
lin_3 <- glm(admit~rank, data = df)
summary(lin_3)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ rank, data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.61490    0.06379   9.640  < 2e-16 ***
## rank        -0.11968    0.02400  -4.987 9.18e-07 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.2049743)
## 
##     Null deviance: 86.677  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 81.580  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 505.2
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2
lin_4 <- glm(admit~gre + gpa, data = df)
summary(lin_4)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ gre + gpa, data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##               Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)  
## (Intercept) -0.5279342  0.2087277  -2.529   0.0118 *
## gre          0.0005489  0.0002141   2.564   0.0107 *
## gpa          0.1542363  0.0649769   2.374   0.0181 *
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.2079531)
## 
##     Null deviance: 86.677  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 82.557  on 397  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 511.96
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2
lin_5 <- glm(admit~rank:gpa, data = df)
summary(lin_5)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ rank:gpa, data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  0.542923   0.062793   8.646  < 2e-16 ***
## rank:gpa    -0.026825   0.006957  -3.856 0.000135 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for gaussian family taken to be 0.2099407)
## 
##     Null deviance: 86.677  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 83.556  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 514.77
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 2
lin_comps <- compare_performance(
  lin_1, lin_2, lin_3, lin_4, lin_5, 
  rank = TRUE)
lin_comps
## # Comparison of Model Performance Indices
## 
## Name  | Model |    R2 |  RMSE | Sigma | AIC weights | AICc weights
## ------------------------------------------------------------------
## lin_3 |   glm | 0.059 | 0.452 | 0.453 |       0.951 |        0.952
## lin_4 |   glm | 0.048 | 0.454 | 0.456 |       0.032 |        0.032
## lin_5 |   glm | 0.036 | 0.457 | 0.458 |       0.008 |        0.008
## lin_1 |   glm | 0.034 | 0.458 | 0.459 |       0.005 |        0.005
## lin_2 |   glm | 0.032 | 0.458 | 0.459 |       0.003 |        0.003
## 
## Name  | BIC weights | Performance-Score
## ---------------------------------------
## lin_3 |       0.979 |           100.00%
## lin_4 |       0.005 |            28.65%
## lin_5 |       0.008 |             8.07%
## lin_1 |       0.005 |             4.26%
## lin_2 |       0.003 |             0.00%
lin_comps %>% plot()

Logistic Modeling

log_1 <- glm(admit~gre, data = df, family = 'binomial')
summary(log_1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ gre, family = "binomial", data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept) -2.901344   0.606038  -4.787 1.69e-06 ***
## gre          0.003582   0.000986   3.633  0.00028 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 499.98  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 486.06  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 490.06
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
log_2 <- glm(admit~gpa, data = df, family = 'binomial')
summary(log_2)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ gpa, family = "binomial", data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)  -4.3576     1.0353  -4.209 2.57e-05 ***
## gpa           1.0511     0.2989   3.517 0.000437 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 499.98  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 486.97  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 490.97
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
log_3 <- glm(admit~rank, data = df, family = 'binomial')
summary(log_3)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ rank, family = "binomial", data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)   0.6366     0.3061   2.080   0.0375 *  
## rank         -0.5863     0.1240  -4.728 2.26e-06 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 499.98  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 475.71  on 398  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 479.71
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
log_4 <- glm(admit~rank + gpa, data = df, family = 'binomial')
summary(log_4)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ rank + gpa, family = "binomial", data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)  -2.8826     1.0916  -2.641 0.008273 ** 
## rank         -0.5822     0.1263  -4.609 4.05e-06 ***
## gpa           1.0270     0.3064   3.352 0.000801 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 499.98  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 463.93  on 397  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 469.93
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 3
log_5 <- glm(admit~rank + gpa + gre, data = df, family = 'binomial')
summary(log_5)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = admit ~ rank + gpa + gre, family = "binomial", 
##     data = df)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept) -3.449548   1.132846  -3.045  0.00233 ** 
## rank        -0.560031   0.127137  -4.405 1.06e-05 ***
## gpa          0.777014   0.327484   2.373  0.01766 *  
## gre          0.002294   0.001092   2.101  0.03564 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 499.98  on 399  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 459.44  on 396  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 467.44
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
log_comps = compare_performance(
  log_1, log_2, log_3, log_4, log_5,
  rank = TRUE)
## Following indices with missing values are not used for ranking: Sigma
log_comps
## # Comparison of Model Performance Indices
## 
## Name  | Model | Tjur's R2 |  RMSE | Sigma | Log_loss | Score_log
## ----------------------------------------------------------------
## log_5 |   glm |     0.099 | 0.442 |     1 |    0.574 |   -50.496
## log_4 |   glm |     0.089 | 0.444 |     1 |    0.580 |   -50.083
## log_3 |   glm |     0.060 | 0.451 |     1 |    0.595 |   -49.032
## log_2 |   glm |     0.032 | 0.458 |     1 |    0.609 |   -48.163

## 
## Name  | Score_spherical |   PCP | AIC weights | AICc weights | BIC weights | Performance-Score
## ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## log_5 |           0.004 | 0.609 |       0.775 |        0.772 |       0.309 |            61.65%
## log_4 |           0.003 | 0.605 |       0.223 |        0.227 |       0.654 |            50.02%
## log_3 |           0.010 | 0.593 |       0.002 |        0.002 |       0.036 |            39.43%
## log_2 |           0.004 | 0.581 |    6.04e-06 |     6.23e-06 |    1.30e-04 |            23.20%
## log_1 |           0.003 | 0.581 |    9.52e-06 |     9.82e-06 |    2.06e-04 |            22.06%
log_comps %>% plot()

Summary

Overall, the best model that I found was a logistic model using admit ~ rank + gpa + gre. It had the best RMSE score.
